climate_change.topic: Climate change: causes, effects and what we can do
key_points: Burning fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas is the main human cause of climate change.
Greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide and methane trap heat and raise global temperatures.
Deforestation and agriculture add to emissions.
Melting ice and warming oceans cause sea levels to rise, threatening coastal areas.
Extreme weather such as heatwaves, droughts and floods is becoming more frequent.
Ecosystems such as coral reefs are damaged by warming.
Poorer countries are often most affected despite contributing least.
Renewable energy and efficiency reduce emissions (mitigation).
Adaptation prepares for unavoidable changes, such as flood defences.
Governments act through carbon pricing and agreements such as the Paris Agreement; individuals can also help.
The brain stays active during sleep; teenagers need about 8-10 hours and adults 7-9.
Sleep consolidates new memories into long-term memory.
Poor sleep reduces attention and the ability to learn the next day.
Lack of sleep worsens mood, reaction time and decision-making.
Sleep supports the immune system and physical health.
Regular sleep times, avoiding screens and caffeine, and a dark quiet room improve sleep.
Spreading revision over days works better than cramming without sleep.
